### Contending for the Faith in a Confused Culture
Author: Justin Dillehay
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/contending-faith-confused-culture/
Passage: Jude 1:3
Points:
- The Christian faith has definite doctrinal boundaries and objective content delivered once for all.
- Apostolic teaching binds together theological truth and moral obligations regarding sin and righteousness.
- Attempting to redefine biblical morality to fit cultural trends constitutes a denial of Christ’s lordship.
- Believing true doctrine and living obediently must never be separated from one another.
- Standing firmly for historic truth amid confusion is the most loving response believers can offer.

### Contending for the Faith - HomeWord - November 4, 2016
Author: Jim Liebelt
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-november-4-2016.html
Passage: Jude 1:3
Points:
- Cultural religion often distorts Christianity into self-serving morality and views God as a distant helper.
- Believers are prone to compromising scriptural boundaries when seeking personal comfort and convenience.
- God revealed Himself personally in Jesus Christ rather than remaining distant and unknowable.
- Genuine faith submits to the living authority of Scripture instead of cultural trends.
- Christians contend for the faith by committing to biblical truth and keeping one another accountable.

### Unbelief and Destruction
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/unbelief-and-destruction
Passage: Jude 1:5-7
Points:
- Jude recounts historical judgments to demonstrate the severe consequences facing false teachers and apostates.
- Although the Israelites were delivered out of Egypt, those lacking saving faith were ultimately destroyed.
- Visible church involvement and external covenant privileges cannot substitute for personal faith in God.
- The judgment of fallen angels and Sodom and Gomorrah serves as an enduring warning against rebellion and sexual immorality.
- Believers must never treat divine grace as permission to indulge in ungodly living.
